name: Cybersecurity Incident
description: A security event involving unauthorized access, malware, ransomware, or other cyber threats to FirstUK Bank systems, data, or infrastructure. This is a top-level incident category requiring coordinated response from Technology and Security teams.

name: Data Breach
description: An incident involving unauthorized access to, disclosure of, or loss of customer or operational data. Requires immediate investigation, regulatory notification, and customer communication.

name: System Outage
description: An unplanned interruption to banking systems, services, or infrastructure affecting customer access or transaction processing. Requires rapid detection, containment, and recovery actions.

name: Operational Failure
description: A failure in banking operational processes, procedures, or controls that impacts service delivery, compliance, or customer outcomes. Covered under the FirstUK Bank Incident Response Plan.

name: Severity 1 (Critical)
description: The highest severity classification for incidents with catastrophic impact — including major financial loss, widespread customer impact, extended system outage, or regulatory breach. Requires immediate escalation and executive notification.

name: Severity 3 (Medium)
description: A medium-severity incident with moderate impact on operations or limited customer scope. Requires investigation and standard escalation procedures.

name: Severity 4 (Low)
description: A low-severity incident with minimal impact on operations or isolated customer effect. Requires documentation and standard handling procedures.

name: Cybersecurity Incident
description: A security event involving malicious software, unauthorized system access, credential compromise, or network-based attacks. Subtypes include malware infection, ransomware attack, unauthorized access, data exfiltration, DDoS attack, and credential compromise. Each subtype has distinct containment and recovery requirements.

name: Data Breach
description: An incident involving unauthorized exposure or access to sensitive data held by the bank. Subtypes include customer personal data exposure, financial data access, system/operational data leakage, and regulatory data breach. Each requires specific notification and remediation protocols.

name: System Incident
description: An operational or technical failure affecting banking systems, data integrity, or service availability. Subtypes include system outage/unavailability, data corruption, performance degradation, integration failure, and backup failure. Recovery procedures vary by subtype and impact scope.

name: Physical Security Incident
description: An incident involving unauthorized physical access to bank facilities, loss or damage to equipment, or failure of physical access controls. Subtypes include facility breach, equipment theft, fire/environmental damage, and access control failure. Requires coordination with physical security and facilities teams.

name: Fraud and Misconduct Incident
description: An incident involving fraudulent activity or misconduct by employees or third parties. Subtypes include unauthorized transactions, employee fraud, and third-party fraud. Requires investigation, potential law enforcement notification, and customer remediation.

name: Severity 1 (Critical)
description: The highest severity classification for incidents with major data breaches affecting over 1,000 customers, ransomware on critical systems, system outages exceeding 4 hours, or regulatory violations. Financial impact threshold exceeds £100,000 and requires immediate escalation and response.
context: Major data breach (personal data exposed, >1,000 customers)
example: Major data breach (personal data exposed, >1,000 customers)

name: Severity 2 (High)
description: High severity classification for suspected data breaches affecting fewer than 1,000 customers, unauthorized access detection, system outages between 1–4 hours, or fraud incidents exceeding £10,000. Financial impact ranges from £10,000 to £100,000.

name: Severity 3 (Medium)
description: Medium severity classification for suspected but unconfirmed unauthorized access, contained malware detection, system performance issues, fraud incidents under £10,000, or policy violations. Financial impact ranges from £1,000 to £10,000.

name: Severity 4 (Low)
description: The lowest severity classification for security alerts that are false positives, minor policy violations, minor system hiccups, or incident reports with no immediate threat. Financial impact is estimated below £1,000.

description: The response action of formally acknowledging and apologizing for the impact of the data breach to affected customers.

name: Severity 1 (Critical)
description: Critical severity level triggered by major system outages, significant financial impact, or widespread customer impact. Requires immediate response with board notification within 2 hours and regulatory notification within 24 hours to the FCA.
examples: Ransomware affecting payment processing system with 4-hour outage and 100+ failed transactions

name: Ransomware Attack
description: A ransomware attack affecting critical banking infrastructure, specifically payment processing systems. This incident type results in system outages, transaction failures, and delayed customer funds with significant financial impact.

name: Cybersecurity Incident
description: Broad category of cybersecurity incidents including ransomware attacks and other malicious activities affecting banking systems and operations.

name: Immediate Response Activation
description: Immediate response activation required for Severity 1 incidents. Triggers urgent containment, investigation, and notification procedures.

name: Board Notification
description: Mandatory notification to the board of directors for Severity 1 incidents, required within 2 hours of incident detection.

name: Regulatory Notification
description: Mandatory notification to the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) for Severity 1 incidents, required within 24 hours of incident detection.

name: Financial Conduct Authority
description: The primary financial regulator for banking incidents in the UK. Must be notified of Severity 1 incidents within 24 hours.

name: Board of Directors
description: Senior executive leadership responsible for strategic incident oversight. Must be notified of Severity 1 incidents within 2 hours.

name: Payment Processing System
description: Critical banking infrastructure responsible for processing customer transactions and fund transfers. Subject to ransomware and other cybersecurity threats.
incident_example: Ransomware attack causing 4-hour outage and 100+ failed transactions

name: Severity 2 (High)
description: High-severity incident affecting a limited customer population with moderate financial impact. Characterized by unauthorized access to customer data affecting up to 50 customers with no evidence of data exfiltration, investigation costs between £10,000–£100,000, and containment within 2 hours. Requires executive team and Chief Risk Officer notification with potential regulatory reporting.
examples: Unauthorized access to customer data with no evidence of exfiltration

name: Unauthorized Access to Customer Data
description: Security incident involving unauthorized access to customer personal data. This incident type is characterized by limited scope (up to 50 customers), absence of confirmed data exfiltration, and rapid containment capability within 2 hours. Triggers executive and regulatory notification requirements.

name: Incident Response Within 2 Hours
description: Mandatory containment action requiring cessation of unauthorized access and stabilization of the incident within 2 hours of detection. This response action is mandatory for Severity 2 incidents involving unauthorized customer data access.

name: Executive Team Notification
description: Mandatory notification to the executive team upon detection of a Severity 2 data access incident. Required as part of the escalation protocol for incidents affecting customer data with moderate financial impact.
trigger_condition: Severity 2 incident with customer data impact

name: Chief Risk Officer Notification
description: Mandatory notification to the Chief Risk Officer upon detection of a Severity 2 data access incident. Required as part of the escalation protocol for incidents involving unauthorized customer data access.
trigger_condition: Severity 2 incident with customer data impact

name: Regulatory Notification Assessment
description: Post-incident assessment action to determine whether regulatory notification is required for a Severity 2 data access incident. The decision is made under assessment based on incident specifics, scope, and regulatory obligations.

name: Severity 3 (Medium)
description: Medium-severity incident classification for contained security events with no system-wide spread or external impact. Requires next business day response with internal notification to department head only. Routine incident handling applies.
examples: Malware detected on staff laptop with endpoint isolation, no system spread

name: Malware Incident
description: Cybersecurity incident involving malware detection on staff endpoint following phishing link click. Characterized by rapid containment through endpoint isolation with no lateral spread to other systems.
subtypes: Phishing link click leading to malware infection

name: Endpoint Isolation and Containment
description: Immediate containment action to isolate infected endpoint from network to prevent lateral spread of malware. Executed as part of routine incident response for Severity 3 cybersecurity events.

name: Department Head Notification
description: Required internal notification to department head for Severity 3 malware incidents. No external notification to regulators, law enforcement, or customers required for contained endpoint incidents.
trigger_condition: Malware incident affecting staff member in department

name: Next Business Day Response
description: Standard response timeline for Severity 3 incidents, allowing resolution within the next business day. Applies to routine, contained security events with no system-wide impact.

name: Detection
description: Initial identification and alerting of security incidents using SIEM, IDS, antivirus, and log aggregation tools. Detection is the first phase of incident response, leveraging automated monitoring systems to identify anomalies and threats.

name: Investigation
description: Deep analysis of detected incidents using forensic tools, memory analysis, packet inspection, and timeline reconstruction. Investigation determines the scope, cause, and impact of security incidents.

name: Real-time Updates Communication
description: Dissemination of incident status and findings to response teams via dedicated Slack channel during active incident response. Enables rapid coordination and information sharing among incident responders.

name: War Room Coordination
description: Establishment of a dedicated video conference for major incident response coordination. War room brings together key stakeholders for synchronous decision-making during critical incidents.
context: War room (video call, during major incidents)

name: External Communication
description: Formal communication with external parties, regulators, and stakeholders regarding incident status and impact. External communication is conducted via email to ensure documented, auditable notification.

name: Incident Response Procedures Training
description: Annual mandatory training for all IT staff covering incident response procedures. This foundational training ensures staff can identify, report, and respond to operational incidents according to established protocols.

name: Forensic Investigation Training
description: Annual specialized training for the security team in forensic investigation techniques. This training prepares the security team to conduct detailed post-incident analysis and evidence collection.

name: Breach Notification Training
description: Annual mandatory training for the compliance team covering breach notification procedures and regulatory requirements. This training ensures the compliance team can execute timely and accurate notifications to regulators and affected customers.

name: Annual Tabletop Exercise
description: Annual simulated incident scenario exercise designed to test response team activation, decision-making under pressure, and communication protocols. This exercise validates the effectiveness of incident response procedures and identifies gaps in team readiness.

name: Information Security Policy
description: Referenced policy document covering preventive security controls and measures. Serves as the foundational reference for security incident prevention and response procedures.

name: Operational Risk Policy
description: Referenced policy document defining incident categorization and operational risk management framework. Provides the taxonomy and classification structure for operational incidents.
topic: Incident categorization and operational risk management

name: Escalation Matrix
description: Reference document defining escalation paths and notification routing for incidents. Specifies which teams and contacts must be notified under different incident scenarios.

name: Incident Log
description: Operational tracking document that records all incidents across the organization. Serves as the authoritative record for incident history and trending analysis.
topic: Tracking and recording of all incidents

name: Incident Response Plan Version 1.1
description: The operational incident response plan document, version 1.1, effective 2026-01-15. This version includes communication templates and supersedes the initial plan from 2025-01-01. The document serves as the authoritative reference for incident detection, containment, investigation, and recovery procedures.

name: Communication Template Development
description: A response action added in version 1.1 of the incident response plan on 2026-01-15. This action establishes standardized communication templates for use during incident response and stakeholder notification.

name: Chief Information Security Officer
description: The Chief Information Security Officer is the author and owner of the incident response plan, responsible for its creation, maintenance, and updates. The CISO authored both version 1.0 (initial plan) and version 1.1 (with communication templates).
context_role: document author and incident response authority
